title: Template structure brainstorm (Quickstarts v1) — folders, naming, env var contract draft
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- We need a stable “template contract” across Python + TypeScript (selective Go later) so docs, CI, and Support don’t have to learn each template separately.
- This is a brainstorm doc. Expect changes.
- Goal: agree on
  (1) repo folder layout
  (2) naming conventions (package names, template IDs, folders)
  (3) env var contract (v1)

Non-goals
- Not trying to build a framework.
- Not trying to support every DB/tool. Start with 1–2.

Open inputs / constraints
- Observability contract v1 wants consistent request_id/tenant/model/route attribution.
- Security wants .env usage documented + secret scanning expectations.
- SRE wants sane defaults: timeouts, retries/backoff, and no alert-noise.
- Docs needs snippet stability (avoid drift).


A) Repo layout options (monorepo)

Option A1 — single monorepo with per-template apps + shared libs
Pros: easiest to keep contract consistent, one CI matrix, easy to share common code (config loader, telemetry wiring).
Cons: can get big, needs clear boundaries to avoid spaghetti.

Proposed:
- redwood-quickstarts/
  - README.md (catalog + “choose your template”)
  - docs/ (optional; repo-level production checklist, release notes)
  - templates/
    - python/
      - rag-fastapi/
      - agents-fastapi/
      - rag-agent-fastapi/
      - _shared/
        - redwood_quickstart/ (config, telemetry, http client wrappers)
    - typescript/
      - rag-express/
      - agents-express/
      - rag-agent-express/
      - _shared/
        - redwood-quickstart/ (config, telemetry, middleware)
  - observability-pack/ (or separate repo; see Option A3)
  - scripts/
    - smoke-test.sh
    - lint-env-docs.js
  - .github/workflows/

Notes:
- Use “_shared” naming to signal internal library (not a template).
- Each template should be runnable with just env vars + a single command.

Option A2 — one repo per template
Pros: very clean boundaries, smaller repos.
Cons: contract drift risk, duplicated CI and shared code, more friction for Docs.

Option A3 — split out the observability pack
- Keep templates in redwood-quickstarts.
- Keep dashboards/alerts in a separate repo (observability-pack) and pin versions.
Pros: avoids coupling dashboard releases to template releases.
Cons: more moving pieces, but might be worth it.

Tentative decision direction (as of 2025-12-16):
- Use A1 for templates + shared libs.
- Use A3 for dashboards/alerts if Sergio wants separate release cadence; otherwise keep as a subtree and later split.


B) Per-template folder skeleton

Principle: “production shape from day one” but still fast to grok.

Python (FastAPI) skeleton (draft)
- templates/python/rag-fastapi/
  - README.md
  - app/
    - main.py (routes)
    - deps.py (DI: client, vector store)
    - api/
      - v1/
        - routes_query.py
        - routes_ingest.py
    - core/
      - config.py (loads env, validates)
      - logging.py (structured logs)
      - telemetry.py (OTel setup)
      - redaction.py (PII guidance + helper)
      - errors.py (error taxonomy)
    - rag/
      - retriever.py
      - prompts.py
      - chunking.py
    - adapters/
      - vectorstore/
        - base.py
        - chroma.py (or pgvector) [TBD backend]
  - worker/
    - ingest_worker.py
    - jobs.py
  - tests/
    - test_smoke.py
    - test_rag_quality.py (minimal)
  - deploy/
    - docker/
      - Dockerfile
      - compose.yaml
    - k8s/
      - deployment.yaml
      - service.yaml
      - hpa.yaml (optional)
  - scripts/
    - run_local.sh

TypeScript (Express) skeleton (draft)
- templates/typescript/rag-express/
  - README.md
  - src/
    - server.ts
    - routes/
      - query.ts
      - ingest.ts
    - core/
      - config.ts
      - logger.ts
      - telemetry.ts
      - redaction.ts
      - errors.ts
    - rag/
      - retriever.ts
      - prompts.ts
      - chunking.ts
    - adapters/
      - vectorstore/
        - base.ts
        - chroma.ts (or pgvector) [TBD]
  - test/
  - deploy/

Notes / nice-to-haves (not required v1)
- Separate “ingest pipeline” process vs “api” process is good for realism; but must support local dev with docker compose.
- Keep deploy assets close to each template (avoid central deploy folder that gets out-of-sync).


C) Naming conventions (template IDs, folders, packages)

1) Template IDs (used in docs, release notes, support)
- Format: <capability>-<runtime>-<language>
Examples:
- rag-fastapi-python
- agents-fastapi-python
- rag-agent-fastapi-python
- rag-express-typescript

Alternative: <language>/<template>
- python/rag-fastapi
- typescript/agents-express

Concern: support tickets and CI benefit from a stable “flat” ID.
Proposed: adopt BOTH
- folder path stays language/template (readable)
- template_id is emitted in telemetry + printed at startup (stable for support)

2) Package/module naming
- Python shared library: redwood_quickstart (underscores) to avoid pip confusion.
- TypeScript shared package folder: redwood-quickstart (dash) but not necessarily published to npm.
- “Quickstart” vs “Quickstarts”: prefer singular in code names.

3) File naming
- Prefer explicit names over abbreviations:
  - telemetry.py/telemetry.ts not otel.py
  - redaction.py not pii.py

4) Headers and correlation IDs naming
- Request ID header: X-Request-Id (common).
- Tenant header: X-Redwood-Tenant (or X-Tenant-Id?)
  - Open question: do we want Redwood-specific header names to reduce collisions?


D) Env var contract (v1 draft)

Goals
- Consistent across templates and languages.
- Minimal set required to run.
- Clear layering: env vars override config file defaults; do not require YAML unless necessary.

Non-goals
- Not a full config system.

Guiding rules
- Prefix with REDWOOD_ for anything related to Redwood platform.
- Prefix with TEMPLATE_ for template-specific toggles (or QUICKSTART_?).
- Prefix with OTEL_ for OpenTelemetry (stick to standard names where possible).
- Avoid env vars that cause high-cardinality metrics by default.

D1) Required Redwood vars
- REDWOOD_API_KEY
  - Required for all templates (Hosted API).
  - Do not print.
- REDWOOD_BASE_URL
  - Default: https://api.redwoodinference.com (placeholder; confirm actual)
  - Purpose: staging/dev override.
- REDWOOD_MODEL
  - Default: a safe/cheap general model (TBD by Product).
- REDWOOD_EMBEDDING_MODEL
  - Default: a known embedding model (TBD).

D2) Request routing / resilience
- REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS
  - Default suggestion: 30000 (30s) for non-streaming; streaming handled separately.
- REDWOOD_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS
  - Default suggestion: 45000 (45s) to cover proxies that kill idle.
- REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES
  - Default: 2 (only safe for idempotent calls; ingestion may be different).
- REDWOOD_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS
  - Default: 250 (with jitter in code).

Note: we may need two retry policies:
- one for model calls
- one for vector DB calls

D3) Telemetry / correlation
- TEMPLATE_ENV
  - Values: local | dev | staging | prod
  - Default: local
- TEMPLATE_SERVICE_NAME
  - Default: redwood-quickstart (but ideally distinct per template)
- TEMPLATE_TEMPLATE_ID
  - Example: rag-fastapi-python
  - Should be constant per template.
- TEMPLATE_VERSION
  - Comes from git tag / build-time var.

Correlation IDs:
- TEMPLATE_TENANT_ID (optional)
  - Used to set default tenant attribute when header is absent.
- TEMPLATE_REQUEST_ID_HEADER
  - Default: X-Request-Id
- TEMPLATE_TENANT_HEADER
  - Default: X-Redwood-Tenant (tentative)

D4) Vector store backend selection (draft)
- TEMPLATE_VECTORSTORE
  - Values: chroma | pgvector (TBD final)
  - Default: chroma for fastest local start? (But enterprise folks ask for pgvector.)
- CHROMA_URL (if chroma)
- PGVECTOR_URL (if pgvector)

Open question: do we force template-specific prefix (TEMPLATE_CHROMA_URL) to avoid env collisions?
- Leaning: use backend-specific conventional names (CHROMA_URL, DATABASE_URL) but document carefully.

D5) RAG tuning knobs (keep minimal)
- TEMPLATE_TOP_K
  - Default: 5
- TEMPLATE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS
  - Default: 2000
- TEMPLATE_CHUNK_SIZE
  - Default: 800
- TEMPLATE_CHUNK_OVERLAP
  - Default: 100

D6) Safety / PII-related toggles (defaults should be safe)
- TEMPLATE_LOG_LEVEL
  - Default: INFO
- TEMPLATE_LOG_REDACT_PII
  - Default: true
- TEMPLATE_ALLOW_UNREDACTED_LOGS
  - Default: false (only for local, with big warning)
- TEMPLATE_TOOL_ALLOWLIST
  - Default: empty unless agents template; in agents template default to a minimal set.


E) Config layering proposal

Motivation: avoid 15 env vars for “hello world”, but still support production.

Proposal (v1)
1) Defaults in code
2) Environment variables override
3) Optional .env for local only (never commit)
4) Optional config file only for Kubernetes / more complex deploys (future)

Add a startup banner (safe):
- prints TEMPLATE_TEMPLATE_ID, TEMPLATE_VERSION, TEMPLATE_ENV
- prints whether telemetry enabled, which vector store backend
- DOES NOT print secrets or full URLs with creds


F) README + docs expectations (what each template must include)

Per-template README sections (consistent headings to help docs snippet extraction)
1) What this template is / what you get
2) Architecture diagram (ASCII ok)
3) Quickstart (local)
4) Configure
   - Table of env vars (include defaults)
5) Observability
   - What metrics/log fields/traces you get
   - How to see it in Redwood Console (deep links if possible)
6) Safety notes
   - PII/logging
   - Tool calling allow-list
7) Deploy
   - Docker Compose
   - Kubernetes (minimal)
8) Troubleshooting
   - 429
   - streaming disconnects
   - timeouts


G) Open questions / parking lot

1) Prefix naming: TEMPLATE_ vs QUICKSTART_
- TEMPLATE_ reads better inside templates.
- QUICKSTART_ might reduce collisions for customers using “template” already.
- Slack thread suggests consistent env vars across languages; decision needed.

2) Base URL naming
- REDWOOD_BASE_URL vs REDWOOD_API_BASE vs REDWOOD_ENDPOINT
- SDKs already have a name; align with Monica/Ibrahim.

3) Tenant header name
- Need standard header(s) for templates so traces join correctly and support can ask “what’s your tenant header”.
- Must align with any existing Redwood headers.

4) Version pinning
- How do we expose SDK version in the template? Should print at startup.

5) Should we provide a “template doctor” script?
- Checks required env vars, network connectivity, and prints actionable errors.
- Might reduce Support tickets.


H) Next steps / TODOs (actionable)
- [Monica] Confirm SDK env var naming / base URL (align with SDK docs).
- [Dana] Propose TypeScript shared core layout (what goes in _shared vs template).
- [Wei] Confirm README heading format needed for docs ingestion.
- [Connor] Draft versioning + TEMPLATE_VERSION injection approach in CI.
- [Talia] Capture decisions from Slack: devex/1734010022 into a short “contract v1” doc once we converge.

Scratch notes (keep for now)
- Don’t put “OBSERVABILITY_” prefix; just use standard OTEL_ env vars + our TEMPLATE_* toggles.
- Avoid making “trace enabled” default false; better to have it on by default with local exporter to console. But need to ensure it doesn’t confuse new users.
- For 429 handling: templates should not set crazy retries; show a clear backoff strategy and budget-aware behavior (stop retrying after N or after total time).
